content: OAuth state-parameter CSRF: a real-world breach involved a state value that was identical for every user/session (not per-session random), letting an attacker's copied auth-URL flow be replayed to link the attacker's account to a victim's session (login CSRF). Correct implementation: cryptographically random per-flow value, stored server-side (or in a short-TTL cookie) tied to the browser that started the flow, compared with constant-time comparison on callback, and invalidated after single use. Login-CSRF/session-fixation variant: attacker starts their own OAuth flow, gets a valid code, and tricks the victim's browser into completing the callback with the attacker's code — binding state to the initiating browser's session (not just a bare random value) is what prevents this.
